notes: 1. Work Progress is a READ-ONLY informational surface on the Buyer portal at https://uat.xrportal.in/work-progress. It shows a project banner, a 'Work Progress' heading, and per-tower tabs; each tower tab shows construction photos with caption text (a Swiper carousel). There are NO forms, tables, comments, uploads, edits, or action buttons — content is published by the developer's team via CMS (BUYER-FS-Work-Progress §1.2 / §1.5; BUYER-FRD Module 11).

2. Buyer auth is Mobile-OTP only (no password). UAT mobile = 8888888888, Buyer OTP = 147258 (portal-specific; the Admin/SM OTP 258369 does NOT work here). Session is a JWT held in sessionStorage. Unauthenticated access to /work-progress redirects to the Buyer login at / (visual-memory INDEX.md Route section).

3. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. a pre-allocation buyer account, a post-allocation buyer account, a CMS state with zero milestones, a captured Buyer JWT, or admin/CMS access to publish/unpublish content).

4. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS or not transcribed in visual-memory; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative. Several lightbox/empty-state/timestamp behaviours below are flagged because the FS describes the feature at a high level only.

5. AVAILABILITY RULE: Work Progress is available to every registered buyer at all journey stages — pre-allocation AND post-allocation (FS §1.5 Rule 3). There is no stage gate; the only precondition is being logged in (FS §1.3).

6. READ-ONLY RULE: buyers cannot add comments or content (FS §1.5 Rule 2). Any input/comment/upload/edit/delete/replace affordance on this page would be a defect. 'No-affordance' assertions below are REQUIRED negative-by-design cases.

7. NOTIFICATION: the FS describes no buyer notification (SMS/WhatsApp/email/in-app) when the developer publishes a new milestone or photo. Buyers discover updates only by visiting the page (and following the FS note to contact their Sales Manager / raise a Support Ticket for stage-specific questions). The 'no notification on new upload' assertion is silence-by-design and is a REQUIRED case.

8. CMS / STRAPI SCOPE: content is sourced from the CMS (Strapi). Per project constraints, Strapi itself is OUT OF SCOPE — do NOT test Strapi directly. CMS-driven cases below verify only the DOWNSTREAM buyer-portal effect (e.g. 'after admin publishes, the buyer sees it on reload'); the admin/Strapi publish step is a precondition/[TEST_DATA_REQUIRED], not an assertion target.

9. GLOSSARY: 'Banner' = the top media block (image/video) with the overlay caption 'See the Vision Come Alive'; 'Work Progress' = the section heading below the banner; 'Tower tab' = a clickable tab naming one building (Crest / Prestige / Triumph / Crown / Horizon / Radiance / Aspire); 'Tower carousel' = the Swiper image slider inside the active tab; 'caption' = the text under each carousel image (e.g. 'Building 4 - view test & Building 5 - view test'); 'sidebar' = the persistent left navigation (Home, Registration, Allotment, Homeloan, Project, Work Progress, Logout).

10. DOC_DRIFT-WP-001 — TOWER TAB COUNT. Live UI (visual-memory work-progress-loaded.png + work-progress-scrolled.png) renders SEVEN tower tabs: Crest, Prestige, Triumph, Crown, Horizon, Radiance, Aspire. The INDEX.md 'Tower / Building Tabs' list also includes an eighth entry 'Preview', which is NOT rendered on screen. Live UI wins: TCs cover the 7 visible towers; 'Preview' is treated as non-rendered / stale and flagged [VERIFY WITH DEV]. (Ant Design renders each tab twice in the DOM — 14 DOM entries for 7 tabs is expected, per INDEX.md note.)

11. DOC_DRIFT-WP-002 — PROJECT NAME. Banner/header on live UI reads 'HoABL Naigaon' (visual-memory screenshots), while INDEX.md headings transcribe 'HoABL Naigaon' as the project h2 — consistent. The top utility bar also shows a marketing strapline 'India's Biggest Growth Housing Revolution Begins On 7th April 2026.' and a 'RERA ID: P99000080006' on the right; neither is documented in BRD/FRD/FS. Live UI wins; these strings are asserted as observed and flagged [VERIFY WITH DEV] for canonical wording.

12. IMPLEMENTATION NOTES carried from the baseline workbook (treat as [VERIFY WITH DEV] unless re-confirmed against current build): the per-buyer tower filter appears to be dead code (every buyer sees ALL towers, not only their allocated tower); projectId is hardcoded to 1 (non-prod still resolves project 1); the tower content uses ISR with an ~10s revalidate window; the banner uses a 'workBannerVideo' config; autoplay continues after manual swipe (disableOnInteraction=false). These are observed/internal behaviours, not BRD/FRD requirements.

13. ID SCHEME: two historical prefixes are preserved verbatim — the BYR_WRK_NNN baseline series and the supplemental TC_WP_<TYPE>_NNN series. New TCs continue the highest number in the appropriate series and NEVER renumber existing IDs. Sub-module banners group TCs in execution order (navigation/landing first, deepest negatives/E2E last).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Work Progress menu item is visible to a logged-in buyer
tcs.description: Verify that the 'Work Progress' item appears in the left sidebar for any logged-in buyer regardless of journey stage.
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in to the Buyer portal (any journey status).
tcs.steps:
1. Log in to the Buyer portal with mobile 8888888888 and OTP 147258.
2. Look at the left navigation sidebar.
tcs.expected: The left sidebar shows a 'Work Progress' item (alongside Home, Registration, Allotment, Homeloan, Project, Logout). It is enabled and clickable for the buyer at any stage.

tcs.scenario: To verify clicking Work Progress navigates to /work-progress
tcs.description: Verify that clicking the sidebar 'Work Progress' item loads the Work Progress page at the correct route.
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in and the sidebar is visible.
tcs.steps:
1. From any page, click 'Work Progress' in the left sidebar.
2. Read the URL bar and the page content.
tcs.expected: The browser navigates to https://uat.xrportal.in/work-progress and the Work Progress page renders with the project banner and the 'Work Progress' heading.

tcs.scenario: To verify the happy-path landing on Work Progress
tcs.description: Verify that a logged-in buyer can open Work Progress and immediately see construction content for the default tower (FS §1.1 objective).
tcs.precond: Buyer is logged in (valid session in fixtures/.auth/buyer.json).
tcs.steps:
1. Log in to the Buyer portal.
2. Click 'Work Progress' in the sidebar.
3. Wait for the page to finish loading.
tcs.expected: Within about 5 seconds the page shows the top banner with the overlay 'See the Vision Come Alive', the 'Work Progress' heading, the row of tower tabs, and the first tower's photo carousel — all without any extra clicks.

tcs.scenario: To verify the project name and section heading render
tcs.description: Verify that the page identifies itself with the project name and the 'Work Progress' section heading, supporting the FS objective of keeping buyers informed about site progress.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Read the heading above the banner and the section heading below it.
tcs.expected: The project name 'HoABL Naigaon' is shown at the top and the section heading 'Work Progress' is shown below the banner. (Source: visual-memory work-progress-loaded.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the top utility bar strapline and RERA ID render
tcs.description: Verify that the top utility bar shows the marketing strapline and the RERA ID observed on the live page.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Read the thin bar across the very top of the page (left and right).
tcs.expected: The top bar shows the strapline 'India's Biggest Growth Housing Revolution Begins On 7th April 2026.' on the left and 'RERA ID: P99000080006' on the right. [VERIFY WITH DEV] DOC_DRIFT-WP-002 — these strings are not in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm canonical wording. (Source: visual-memory screenshots.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the page header / title is rendered
tcs.description: Verify that the Work Progress page renders its header/title area without a broken or blank header.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Observe the header area at the top of the content.
tcs.expected: The header area renders cleanly with the project name and the 'Work Progress' section title — no blank header, no missing/placeholder title text.

tcs.scenario: To verify the top banner media renders with its overlay caption
tcs.description: Verify that the top banner (image/video) renders with the overlay caption 'See the Vision Come Alive'.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. The CMS banner media is configured. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CMS banner populated.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Look at the large media block at the top of the page.
tcs.expected: The banner media displays a construction-site visual with the centred overlay caption 'See the Vision Come Alive'. If the banner is a video it plays muted and looped with no visible player controls. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether the banner is served as an image or an autoplay video is build-dependent; confirm. (Source: visual-memory work-progress-loaded.png; baseline 'workBannerVideo' note.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the banner caption text is the configured value
tcs.description: Verify that the banner overlay caption text matches the value configured for the banner (downstream of CMS).
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CMS banner caption configured.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Read the overlay text on the banner.
tcs.expected: The banner overlay reads 'See the Vision Come Alive' as observed live. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not specify the banner caption string; confirm it is the canonical configured value. (CMS/Strapi itself is out of scope — assert only the rendered text.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a banner media update surfaces to the buyer after the revalidate window
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that a banner media update published in CMS appears on the buyer page after a reload past the revalidate window.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. Admin updates the banner media in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access to change the banner.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current banner.
2. Have admin publish a new banner media in CMS.
3. Wait past the revalidate window (~10s) and reload /work-progress.
tcs.expected: After the revalidate window the buyer sees the updated banner on reload. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the ~10s ISR revalidate is an implementation note, not a BRD/FRD requirement; confirm the propagation window. (Strapi out of scope — verify buyer-side render only.)

tcs.scenario: To verify each tower in the project is shown as a tab
tcs.description: Verify that the project's towers are each represented as a selectable tab in the Work Progress section.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Look at the row of tabs below the 'Work Progress' heading.
tcs.expected: Seven tower tabs are shown in order: 'Crest', 'Prestige', 'Triumph', 'Crown', 'Horizon', 'Radiance', 'Aspire'. (Source: visual-memory work-progress-scrolled.png. DOC_DRIFT-WP-001: INDEX.md also lists 'Preview' which is NOT rendered — see TC_WP_UI_006.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the 'Preview' tab listed in docs is not rendered
tcs.description: Verify the documented tower-tab list against the live UI, recording that the eighth 'Preview' entry from INDEX.md does not render.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Count and read every tower tab.
tcs.expected: Only seven tabs render (Crest, Prestige, Triumph, Crown, Horizon, Radiance, Aspire); no 'Preview' tab is present. DOC_DRIFT-WP-001 — INDEX.md lists 'Preview' as an eighth tab; live UI wins. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether 'Preview' is intentionally hidden/removed or stale documentation.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tower tab is active by default on first landing
tcs.description: Verify that on first landing one tower tab is pre-selected so progress content is visible without extra clicks (FS §1.1).
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; first visit to /work-progress in the session.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress for the first time in the session.
2. Observe which tab is highlighted and whether its content panel is populated.
tcs.expected: The first tab ('Crest') is active/highlighted by default and its photo carousel is already populated on landing. (Source: visual-memory work-progress-scrolled.png shows 'Crest' active.)

tcs.scenario: To verify switching tabs replaces the visible content panel
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a different tower tab replaces the content panel so the buyer sees the correct tower's photos.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with the default tab active.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the content under the active 'Crest' tab.
2. Click the 'Prestige' tab.
3. Compare the content panel.
tcs.expected: Clicking a different tab makes it the active tab and replaces the content panel with that tower's photos/captions; the previous tower's content is no longer shown.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tower added/removed in CMS appears/disappears as a tab
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that adding or removing a tower in CMS changes the rendered set of tower tabs on reload.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. Admin adds or removes a tower entry in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access to add/remove a tower.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current tower tabs.
2. Have admin add a new tower (or remove an existing one) in CMS.
3. Wait past the revalidate window and reload /work-progress.
tcs.expected: On reload the new tower appears as an additional tab (or the removed tower's tab disappears). [VERIFY WITH DEV] propagation timing (~10s ISR). (Strapi out of scope — verify buyer-side tab set only.)

tcs.scenario: To verify every buyer sees ALL towers (no per-buyer tower filter)
tcs.description: Verify that the buyer is shown all towers, not only the tower of their allocated unit.
tcs.precond: A buyer allocated to a single tower (e.g. Crest) is logged in. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a post-allocation buyer tied to one tower.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a buyer allocated to one tower.
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Look at the set of tower tabs.
tcs.expected: All seven tower tabs are shown — the view is NOT filtered to the buyer's allocated tower. [VERIFY WITH DEV] baseline note indicates the per-buyer tower filter is dead code; confirm this is intended (every buyer sees all towers).

tcs.scenario: To verify the active tower lists construction photos
tcs.description: Verify that the active tower tab shows at least one construction photo when content is published (FS §1.4).
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. CMS has at least one published photo for the active tower. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] published photo.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Look at the content panel under the active tower tab.
tcs.expected: The active tower shows one or more construction photos in a carousel, each with caption text below it (FS §1.4 'Construction milestone photos').

tcs.scenario: To verify tower photos load without a 404 / broken image
tcs.description: Verify that the photos in the active tower carousel load fully and show no broken-image icons.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with photos present.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Inspect each photo in the active tower carousel.
tcs.expected: Every photo renders fully — no broken-image icon, no blank box, no 404 placeholder.

tcs.scenario: To verify the stage/caption description text renders per photo
tcs.description: Verify that each photo shows its stage/description caption (FS §1.4 'Progress updates').
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with photos present.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Read the caption text under each photo in the active tower.
tcs.expected: Each photo has a caption describing the stage (e.g. 'Building 4 - view test & Building 5 - view test'). (Source: visual-memory work-progress-scrolled.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a milestone/date label is shown where provided
tcs.description: Verify that, where the CMS provides a milestone date, it is displayed against the relevant photo/stage (FS §1.4 'Milestone dates').
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. CMS content includes a milestone date. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] content with a date.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Look for a date label near each photo/stage.
tcs.expected: Where a milestone date is configured it is shown against the relevant photo/stage. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the live captures show caption text but no explicit date label; confirm whether dates are rendered and the date format. (FS §1.4 lists 'Milestone dates'.)

tcs.scenario: To verify milestones render in chronological order
tcs.description: Verify that multiple milestones/photos appear in a sensible chronological order within a tower.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. The active tower has multiple milestones. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] multiple milestones.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress on a tower with several milestones.
2. Note the order of the photos/stages.
tcs.expected: Milestones appear in chronological order (earliest to latest, or as ordered in CMS). [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not state an explicit ordering rule; confirm the intended order is chronological / CMS-defined.

tcs.scenario: To verify the tower photo carousel is navigable
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer can move through the photos in a tower's carousel (swipe / arrows / dots).
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. The active tower has multiple photos. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] tower with >=2 photos.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress on a tower with multiple photos.
2. Advance the carousel (swipe, arrow, or pagination dot).
3. Observe the photo change.
tcs.expected: The carousel advances to the next photo and its caption; the buyer can navigate forward and back through all photos in the tower.

tcs.scenario: To verify the carousel shows the correct number of images per breakpoint
tcs.description: Verify that the carousel adapts how many images it shows per view across responsive breakpoints.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. A tower has >=4 images. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] tower with >=4 images.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress at desktop width on a tower with >=4 images.
2. Resize the browser narrower and wider.
3. Note how many images are visible per view at each width.
tcs.expected: The number of images shown per view adjusts at the responsive breakpoints (more per view on wider screens, fewer on narrow). [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact slidesPerView values per breakpoint are an implementation detail; confirm the configured values.

tcs.scenario: To verify the carousel layout at a tablet (~768px) viewport
tcs.description: Verify that the tower carousel shows the correct slidesPerView and layout at a tablet width.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Resize the browser to ~768px width.
2. Open /work-progress and view a tower carousel.
tcs.expected: The carousel renders the tablet-breakpoint number of images per view with no overlap or clipping and the captions stay legible. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the exact tablet slidesPerView value.

tcs.scenario: To verify autoplay continues after a manual swipe
tcs.description: Verify that, if the carousel autoplays, manual interaction does not permanently stop autoplay (disableOnInteraction=false).
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with an autoplaying tower carousel. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] tower with multiple images.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress and watch the carousel autoplay.
2. Manually swipe to a different image.
3. Wait and observe whether autoplay resumes.
tcs.expected: After the manual swipe the carousel resumes autoplaying. [VERIFY WITH DEV] autoplay + disableOnInteraction=false is a baseline implementation note, not a BRD/FRD requirement; confirm autoplay is enabled and resumes.

tcs.scenario: To verify long caption text is handled gracefully
tcs.description: Verify that an over-long caption is truncated/wrapped (e.g. ellipsis) rather than breaking the card layout.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. A tower image has a caption longer than ~150 chars. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] long-caption content.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress on a tower whose image has a very long caption.
2. Observe how the caption renders under the image.
tcs.expected: The long caption is truncated or wrapped cleanly (e.g. 2-line ellipsis) without overflowing or distorting the card/carousel layout. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not specify a truncation rule; confirm the intended overflow behaviour.

tcs.scenario: To verify clicking a photo opens an enlarged view
tcs.description: Verify whether clicking a construction photo opens an enlarged view / lightbox.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with a photo visible.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Click a photo in the active tower carousel.
3. Observe whether an enlarged view opens.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not document a lightbox. Confirm whether clicking a photo opens an enlarged/lightbox view; if it does, the enlarged image renders without distortion. If clicking does nothing, record 'no lightbox — by design'. (Live captures do not show a lightbox state.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the enlarged view closes on X or ESC
tcs.description: Verify that, if a lightbox exists, it closes via its X control and via the ESC key.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; an enlarged photo / lightbox is open (depends on BYR_WRK_011). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] lightbox present.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the enlarged photo view.
2. Click the X / close control.
3. Re-open it and press ESC.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] dependent on a lightbox existing (BYR_WRK_011). If present, the lightbox closes on both the X control and the ESC key, returning focus to the page. If no lightbox exists, mark N/A.

tcs.scenario: To verify the empty state when no content is published
tcs.description: Verify that the page shows a graceful empty state (not an error) when the CMS has no published milestones/photos.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; CMS has zero published milestones/photos. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CMS/tower state with no content.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress for a tower with no published content.
2. Observe the content panel.
tcs.expected: The page renders without crashing and shows a graceful empty/placeholder state instead of photos. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not specify the empty-state text; confirm the exact wording (e.g. a 'no updates yet' message).

tcs.scenario: To verify a progressive placeholder while photos load
tcs.description: Verify that slow-loading photos show a placeholder/skeleton rather than a blank gap.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with the network throttled to 3G.
tcs.steps:
1. Throttle the network to 3G in DevTools.
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Observe the photo area while images load.
tcs.expected: While images load the carousel shows a progressive placeholder/skeleton (or low-res blur) and then resolves to full images. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not specify a loading placeholder; confirm the intended loading affordance.

tcs.scenario: To verify a single broken image does not break the carousel
tcs.description: Verify that one image returning 404 does not prevent the rest of the tower carousel from rendering.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. One image in a tower returns 404. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a tower with one broken image URL.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress on a tower where one image URL is broken.
2. Navigate through the carousel.
tcs.expected: The broken image shows a placeholder/skips gracefully and the remaining photos still render and remain navigable; the carousel does not crash.

tcs.scenario: To verify the page renders when the tower-gallery content is missing
tcs.description: Verify that the page still renders if the CMS response omits the tower-gallery content block.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. CMS returns a response without the tower-gallery component. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CMS response missing tower-gallery.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress when the tower-gallery block is absent from the CMS response.
2. Observe the page.
tcs.expected: The page renders the banner/heading/tabs and shows an empty/placeholder content area instead of throwing an error or a blank page. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the intended fallback. (Strapi out of scope — verify buyer-side resilience only.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a graceful fallback when the content service is down
tcs.description: Verify that a CMS/content outage shows a graceful fallback rather than a crashed page.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; the content service is simulated down. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to simulate a content-service outage.
tcs.steps:
1. Simulate the content service being unavailable (block its requests in DevTools).
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Observe the page.
tcs.expected: The page does not white-screen; it shows a graceful fallback / placeholder. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the FS does not document outage behaviour; confirm the intended fallback message and that no raw error is exposed.

tcs.scenario: To verify the loading placeholder behaviour when content never resolves
tcs.description: Verify what the buyer sees when the content service is blocked so tower data never loads.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; the content service URL is blocked in the network. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to block the content URL.
tcs.steps:
1. Block the content/Strapi URL in DevTools.
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Wait and observe the tower content area.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] baseline note reports a 'Loading tower data...' placeholder that persists indefinitely with no timeout/retry. Confirm whether this indefinite-loading state is acceptable or should fall back to an error/empty state. (Potential UX gap — flag, do not assert Pass without confirmation.)

tcs.scenario: To verify no comment / edit affordance is rendered

tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:

2. Scan the whole page for any comment box, reply field, rating, or edit control.
tcs.expected: No comment field, reply box, rating, or edit control is present anywhere on the page — the page is purely informational (FS §1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify no input/upload/edit affordance exists anywhere
tcs.description: Verify the read-only business rule by confirming there is no input, comment, upload, or edit affordance on the page.

1. Open /work-progress.
2. Inspect the banner, tabs, every photo card, and the page chrome for any actionable input control.
tcs.expected: The page contains only navigation (tabs, carousel controls, sidebar) and display content — no text inputs, file pickers, comment areas, or save/submit buttons (FS §1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify no upload/replace photo control is rendered
tcs.description: Verify that no upload or replace-photo control appears on any milestone/photo card.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:

2. Hover and inspect each photo card for an upload/replace control.
tcs.expected: No upload, replace, or 'change photo' control is present on any card — buyers cannot add or alter photos (FS §1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with cards present.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Hover and inspect each card for a delete/remove/trash control.
tcs.expected: No delete, remove, or trash control is present on any milestone/photo card (FS §1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.description: Verify whether the page shows any 'last updated' / freshness timestamp on the carousel.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; the tower carousel is visible.
tcs.steps:

2. Look for any 'last updated' / timestamp text near the carousel or cards.

tcs.scenario: To verify normal image consumption (right-click save) is not blocked
tcs.description: Verify that buyers can consume images normally — read-only does not mean images are DRM-locked.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress with a photo visible.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Right-click a construction photo.
3. Observe the browser context menu.
tcs.expected: The standard browser context menu appears (e.g. 'Save image as') — image consumption is not artificially blocked. [VERIFY WITH DEV] no requirement either way; confirm there is no intentional right-click suppression.

tcs.scenario: To verify the context menu exposes no admin/authoring actions
tcs.description: Verify that the browser context menu over the page exposes no custom admin or authoring actions.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /work-progress.
2. Right-click on photos, captions, and tabs.
tcs.expected: Only the standard browser context menu appears; no custom 'edit', 'publish', 'delete', or other admin/authoring actions are exposed to the buyer.

tcs.scenario: To verify Work Progress is available pre- and post-allocation
tcs.description: Verify that Work Progress is reachable and renders for a buyer in any journey state (FS §1.5 Rule 3).
tcs.precond: A buyer account in any journey state is logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a buyer (any stage).
2. Open /work-progress.
tcs.expected: The Work Progress page renders fully for the buyer regardless of stage — no 'not available yet' gate (FS §1.5 Rule 3).

tcs.scenario: To verify no stage gate blocks pre-allocation buyers
tcs.description: Verify that a pre-allocation buyer (no unit allocated) has the same Work Progress access as a post-allocation buyer.
tcs.precond: Two buyer sessions are available — one pre-allocation and one post-allocation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] both buyer states (if only one is available, document the other as not-tested).
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as the pre-allocation buyer and open /work-progress.
2. Log in as the post-allocation buyer and open /work-progress.
3. Compare access and rendered content.
tcs.expected: Both buyers reach /work-progress and see the full banner + tabs + tower content; access is identical with no stage-based restriction (FS §1.5 Rule 3).

tcs.scenario: To verify a newly published milestone appears on reload
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that content published in CMS becomes visible to the buyer after reload.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. Admin publishes a new milestone in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current content.
2. Have admin publish a new milestone in CMS.
3. Wait past the revalidate window and reload /work-progress.
tcs.expected: On reload the new milestone (photo + caption) appears in the relevant tower. (Strapi out of scope — verify buyer-side render only; propagation timing per BYR_WRK_037.)

tcs.scenario: To verify an unpublished milestone disappears on reload
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that content removed in CMS is no longer shown to the buyer after reload.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. Admin unpublishes a milestone in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note an existing milestone.
2. Have admin unpublish it in CMS.
3. Wait past the revalidate window and reload /work-progress.
tcs.expected: On reload the unpublished milestone is no longer displayed in the tower.

tcs.scenario: To verify an edited description is reflected on reload
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that an edited caption/description in CMS is reflected to the buyer after reload.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress. Admin edits a milestone description in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current caption text.
2. Have admin edit the description in CMS.
3. Wait past the revalidate window and reload /work-progress.
tcs.expected: On reload the updated caption/description text is shown against the photo.

tcs.scenario: To verify the revalidate window is honoured for new content
tcs.description: Verify that new content surfaces after the revalidate window rather than only on a hard cache clear.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in. Admin publishes new content at time T. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access + timing.
tcs.steps:
1. Have admin publish new tower content at T.
2. Reload /work-progress just after the revalidate window (~10s).
tcs.expected: The new content surfaces on the reload after the revalidate window. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the ~10s ISR revalidate is an implementation note, not a BRD/FRD requirement; confirm the actual window.

tcs.scenario: To verify reordered images propagate after revalidate
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that reordering images in CMS changes their order for the buyer after revalidate.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in. Admin reorders tower images in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current image order.
2. Have admin reorder the images in CMS.
3. Reload /work-progress after the revalidate window.
tcs.expected: On reload the images appear in the new order. [VERIFY WITH DEV] propagation timing.

tcs.scenario: To verify a caption update propagates after revalidate
tcs.description: Verify the downstream effect that a caption edit in CMS propagates to the buyer after the revalidate window.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in. Admin edits an image caption in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current caption.
2. Have admin edit the caption in CMS.
3. Reload /work-progress after the revalidate window.
tcs.expected: On reload the updated caption text is shown. [VERIFY WITH DEV] propagation timing.

tcs.scenario: To verify project resolution (projectId) for content
tcs.description: Verify which project's content the buyer sees, given the baseline note that projectId is hardcoded to 1.
tcs.precond: A buyer allocated to a project other than project 1 is logged in. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer on project != 1.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a buyer tied to a project other than 1.
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Observe whose project content is shown.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] baseline note states projectId is hardcoded to 1 — confirm whether all buyers see project 1's content regardless of their own project, or whether content is resolved per the buyer's project. This determines correctness for multi-project rollouts. (Potential defect — flag, do not assert Pass without confirmation.)

tcs.scenario: To verify no notification is sent when new content is published
tcs.description: Verify the silence-by-design rule that publishing new content sends the buyer no SMS/WhatsApp/email/in-app notification (FS does not define one).
tcs.precond: Buyer account exists. Admin publishes a new tower image/milestone in CMS. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin/CMS access + ability to observe buyer notification channels.
tcs.steps:
1. Have admin publish new Work Progress content in CMS.
2. Check the buyer's SMS, WhatsApp, email, and in-app notification channels.
tcs.expected: No SMS, WhatsApp, email, or in-app notification is dispatched to the buyer for the new content — discovery is by visiting the page only (silence-by-design; FS defines no notification). This 'no notification' assertion is required, not optional.

tcs.scenario: To verify the page is responsive on a mobile viewport
tcs.description: Verify that the Work Progress page renders without horizontal overflow on a small mobile viewport.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. Resize the browser to a mobile width (<=480px).
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Check the banner, tabs, and carousel.
tcs.expected: All sections (banner, tower tabs, carousel, captions) render within the viewport with no horizontal scroll; tabs remain tappable and the carousel remains swipeable.

tcs.scenario: To verify the page at the captured 1920x900 desktop baseline
tcs.description: Verify that the page matches the captured desktop layout at the documented viewport.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; browser at 1920x900.
tcs.steps:
1. Set the browser to 1920x900.
2. Open /work-progress.
3. Compare against the captured baseline.
tcs.expected: The layout matches visual-memory work-progress-loaded.png — banner with 'See the Vision Come Alive', 'Work Progress' heading, the seven tower tabs, and the first tower carousel, all aligned with no clipping.

tcs.scenario: To verify the buyer can navigate away via the sidebar
tcs.description: Verify that the persistent left sidebar lets the buyer leave Work Progress for another section.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. On /work-progress, click another sidebar item (e.g. 'Home').
2. Observe the navigation.
tcs.expected: The sidebar remains visible on /work-progress and clicking another item navigates the buyer away to that section (e.g. Home), confirming the page is part of the standard authenticated shell.

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout from Work Progress ends the session
tcs.description: Verify that logging out from the Work Progress view terminates the session so protected URLs require re-authentication.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; on /work-progress.
tcs.steps:
1. On /work-progress, click 'Logout' in the sidebar.
2. After redirect, try to navigate back to /work-progress.
tcs.expected: Logout clears the client session and redirects to the Buyer login at /; navigating back to /work-progress redirects to login (the protected page does not render).

tcs.scenario: To verify an unauthenticated actor cannot view Work Progress
tcs.description: Verify that /work-progress is gated — with no session it redirects to login and exposes no content.
tcs.precond: No buyer session — storage cleared, no cookies/tokens for uat.xrportal.in.
tcs.steps:
1. In a fresh/incognito browser with no session, navigate directly to https://uat.xrportal.in/work-progress.
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: The app redirects to the Buyer login at /; the Work Progress page does not render and no construction content is exposed (visual-memory INDEX.md: unauthenticated access redirects to /).

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered/expired JWT cannot view Work Progress
tcs.description: Verify that an invalid or expired session token is rejected and the buyer is sent to login.
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; the sessionStorage JWT can be edited. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to tamper/expire the JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools, Application, sessionStorage.
2. Alter a character in the stored JWT (or use an expired token).
3. Reload /work-progress.
tcs.expected: The session is rejected and the buyer is redirected to the Buyer login at /; no protected content loads. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the exact at-expiry behaviour and whether redirect vs 401 is surfaced are not documented in BRD/FRD; confirm.

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer write to the content store is rejected
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer cannot mutate Work Progress content via a direct write to the content backend.
tcs.precond: A captured Buyer JWT is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] captured Buyer JWT + API client.
tcs.steps:
1. With the Buyer JWT, attempt a PUT/PATCH to the content endpoint that serves Work Progress data.
2. Observe the response.
tcs.expected: The write is rejected (401/403) — buyers have read-only access and cannot edit content. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the content store is the CMS (Strapi, out of scope to test directly); confirm the buyer-facing API enforces read-only and record the exact rejection code.

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer cannot inject a milestone via direct API call
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer cannot create Work Progress content via a direct POST to the content backend.
tcs.precond: A captured Buyer JWT is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] captured Buyer JWT + API client.
tcs.steps:
1. With the Buyer JWT, attempt a POST to create a milestone/photo on the content endpoint.
2. Observe the response.
tcs.expected: The create is rejected (401/403) — buyers cannot inject content. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the buyer-facing API rejects writes and record the exact code. (Strapi out of scope to test directly.)

tcs.scenario: To verify no buyer-facing comment endpoint exists
tcs.description: Verify that there is no accessible comment/authoring API for the buyer on Work Progress (consistent with the read-only UI).
tcs.precond: A captured Buyer JWT is available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] captured Buyer JWT + API client.
tcs.steps:
1. With the Buyer JWT, attempt to call any comment/feedback endpoint associated with Work Progress.
2. Observe the response.
tcs.expected: No comment/authoring endpoint is available for the buyer (404/403); the read-only UI has no API counterpart for authoring. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no such endpoint exists.

tcs.scenario: To verify the full browse-all-towers journey
tcs.description: Verify the complete buyer journey: log in, open Work Progress, view the banner, and browse every tower tab's content in turn (FS How-to Steps 1-2).
tcs.precond: Buyer logged in; CMS has content for the towers. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] published content for multiple towers.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in to the Buyer portal (8888888888 / 147258).
2. Click 'Work Progress' in the sidebar.
3. View the banner and the default tower's photos.
4. Click through each tower tab (Crest, Prestige, Triumph, Crown, Horizon, Radiance, Aspire) and view each tower's carousel.
5. Navigate away via the sidebar.
tcs.expected: The buyer reaches /work-progress, sees the banner and 'Work Progress' heading, and can open each of the seven tower tabs in turn — each showing that tower's photos and captions — then navigate away cleanly via the sidebar. No errors at any step.

tcs.expected: The Crest tab becomes active and its photo carousel + captions render (Crest is the default first tab per visual-memory).
